# Sections

* [app/](app/) - What the designer app in app/ implements, module by module: build status per roadmap phase, the scripting surface (app.exec), garment cutting from curves, pattern pieces and flattening.
* [architecture/](architecture/) - System-level structure of the product: what the POC provides, the garment data model, and how role views sit on one design.
* [geometry/](geometry/) - Geometry techniques for designing a leotard directly on the body and turning it into production pattern pieces: surface layer instead of cloth simulation, body models, curves and panels on surfaces, flattening with stretch compensation, surface addresses, stone distribution, collision checks, size transfer and library options.
* [pipeline/](pipeline/) - Offline tooling that produces the POC's assets: the Blender + MPFB 2 script that bakes the shared-topology mannequin bodies from the CC0 MakeHuman base mesh.
* [platform/](platform/) - Every rendering engine and platform option evaluated in the research, its status after the owner's decisions (three.js chosen; native desktop plus iPad), and the browser, packaging and licence facts behind them.
* [poc/](poc/) - What the three.js proof of concept in poc-threejs/ actually implements, module by module, with its shortcuts and what a production version would need.
* [rendering/](rendering/) - How fabrics and sparkle are drawn in real time: fabric shading recipes and the glitter, spangle and crystal techniques.
* [ux/](ux/) - How the editor should feel and behave: the Dressmaker build loop, painting and sculpting tool models, creativity-tool principles and the stone-placement interaction model.
